title: A very short initial speech unit finishes before the next longer unit is generated
symptom: A normal-entry cold start on the dedicated API34 ARM64 emulator plays a five-character first unit, then leaves a measured 2.849771-second internal silent interval before a forty-character first unit in the next chapter. The source is normally imported cold-short.txt; the previous process is force-stopped and confirmed absent before launching the app and starting listening through the reader.
root_cause: Before the fix, the service only requested upcoming audio after onUtteranceStarted. The initial unit has no earlier playing unit to provide preparation time: its 949ms PCM ends well before the following unit's 3646ms synthesis completes. The two-future-unit queue fixes steady playback lookahead but cannot create startup lead for this short head. Native generation is serialized, while AudioTrack playback does not hold the native mutex; generation/playback mutual exclusion is not the cause. Moving the request slightly ahead of the first-frame callback alone cannot cover this roughly 2.7-second supply deficit.
fix: Implemented and verified for the covered startup defect: only initial or rebuilt playback supplies a lazy successor callback. After generating the current PCM, ReaderTtsAudioPreparation.takeForPlayback divides its duration by the actual clamped playback rate. It waits for the next PCM only when that playback duration is below two seconds and the successor has more than twice as many Unicode characters. This is a conservative rule for an observed tiny-head case, not a general prediction of device throughput.

The service resolves the successor on demand, including the next non-empty chapter when starting at a chapter tail. An ordinary initial PCM of at least two seconds does not invoke this callback or wait for extra chapter IO. Similar short successors do not trigger the audio barrier. Voice preview and ongoing segment transitions retain the ordinary speak entry point.

The barrier joins the matching pending audio without taking it, so the later normal consumer receives the same PCM without another synthesis. An existing matching two-unit window is retained, and bounded ordered preparation remains limited to two future units; no full-chapter audio buffer or prediction framework is added. A successor synthesis failure remains deferred until that unit is consumed.

Pause and stop invalidate the playback epoch and cancel the current consumer before clearing pending preparation. This order prevents cancellation of the pending Deferred from releasing a still-current startup barrier. Existing session tokens, focus gates, preparation watchdog and timer-start-at-actual-playback boundaries remain in force. Waiting is cancellable; native cancellation may still finish at its existing callback boundary.

Added playStart and playEnd logs with utterance, chapter, source offset, character count and elapsedRealtime. playStart is emitted when playback-head progress is observed, not when track.play is called. Generation completion now includes chapter, offset and elapsedRealtime to align native preparation, AudioTrack boundaries and the captured output.

The fix retains ZipVoice-Distill INT8, four threads, three steps, the full 6.057-second reference, existing text segmentation and playback-rate handling. It adds initial waiting only for the narrow short-head case, allowing its first two units to play without the confirmed generation wait between them. In the formal candidate cold start, the reader click at 16:27:08.053 precedes the first playStart at 16:27:19.296 by 11.243 seconds, including model preparation, head synthesis and the initial successor buffer. This is the measured total startup cost for that run, not a universal latency or a paired startup-improvement claim.
evidence: 2026-10-16 formal baseline reproduction: normal reader action at 15:39:47; model ready at 15:39:53.167. Chapter 0 / offset 0 / five characters completes synthesis at 15:39:54.855, taking 1657ms for 949ms of audio. Chapter 1 / offset 0 / forty characters only begins synthesis at 15:39:54.963 and completes at 15:39:58.610, taking 3646ms for 8501ms of audio.

The full baseline internal-output recording contains an independently scanned 2.849771-second interval between the short initial unit and its longer successor. Native timings independently establish inadequate preparation lead; this is actual output evidence, not just a PLAYING state or a successful model call.

Existing ReaderOfflineListeningTest coverage starts with a normal 36-character unit and an eight-character tail. That covered steady cross-chapter preparation but did not exercise cold short-head-to-long-successor startup. ReaderTtsSegmenter may combine natural paragraphs inside its forty-character window, so future reproductions must identify the actual spoken units rather than infer their length from paragraph breaks.

Unified verification passes 347 JVM tests, 30 direct device tests including 14 controlled-engine service regressions, and a separate five-test real-engine group. The JVM coverage includes the initial barrier, no successor lookup on ordinary starts, retaining an existing two-unit window, playback-rate-aware selection and similar-length bypass, cancellation, and deferred successor failure. The service coverage includes cross-chapter startup pause/resume and stop without late playback. The 14 controlled-engine cases are included in the 30-test direct group; controlled-engine success alone does not prove actual audio output.

Formal normal-entry candidate cold start, /private/tmp/story-app-experience-20261016/cold-short-candidate.mka: the same five-character to forty-character handoff has 949ms of head PCM and a successor taking 4030ms to generate 8501ms of PCM. The successor is ready at 16:27:19.200 before the head's actual playStart at 16:27:19.296. The recording reports an internal low-level interval of 0.314562 seconds at 55.709312-56.023875 seconds, compared with the baseline 2.849771-second supply gap. The removed generation wait is established by the completed successor preceding actual head playback as well as by the recorded output.

The candidate uses raw PCM in timestamp-preserving Matroska rather than concatenated PCM. A calibration with an intentional 5.063-second pause followed by 2.649 seconds of resume generation corresponds approximately to a 7.5575-second recorded idle interval, confirming that this capture retains real idle time. Earlier FLAC capture timestamps have jitter and are excluded from the final B audio evidence; sample concatenation or silently rewriting timestamps must not be used to hide gaps.

A second complete short cold-start recording, /private/tmp/story-app-experience-20261016/startup-cancel-controls.mka, has no internal low-level interval of at least 0.6 seconds across actual speech at 24.069-55.106 seconds. Its filename is historical: this recording contains uninterrupted complete playback, not cancellation-control evidence.

Separate formal buffer controls are evidenced by buffer-pause-logcat and buffer-stop-logcat in /private/tmp/story-app-experience-20261016: the user taps pause 86ms and stop 146ms after successor synthesis begins. After eight seconds the respective UI states remain paused and stopped, without spontaneous playback. The separate buffer-controls.mka capture spans 85.99 seconds with a maximum level of -91dB and contains no emitted speech. This covers actual preparation cancellation in addition to the fake-service regressions.

The user listened to both formal fixed representative recordings at 1x and 1.45x and confirmed no obvious sound defects on 2026-10-16. This passes subjective quality for those fixed samples, not arbitrary text. The 1x recording separately contains a 0.923208-second handoff gap under investigation; its successor PCM was already ready. The fifteen-minute formal run is being verified separately. These broader checks do not change the resolved short-initial-unit supply scope.

This record belongs to the approved 2026-10-16 experience-stability work. The main execution evidence and eventual candidate identity are maintained in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-16-app-experience-stability.md; BUG-2026-056 covers the earlier steady short-tail lookahead defect, and BUG-2026-062 retains the separate real-device thermal and sustained-throughput limits.
impact: Resolved within the measured short-initial-unit supply scope: normal-entry candidate recordings and generation/playback timing show the successor ready before the short head starts, removing the baseline 2.849771-second generation wait; actual buffering-period pause and stop do not later emit speech. Startup buffering exchanges some initial waiting for continuity and cannot make fixed generation cost disappear. The status does not close the overall experience audit or establish fixed-sample and fifteen-minute acceptance, sustained performance on arbitrary text, hot-state or physical-phone behavior, battery/temperature improvement, or subjective voice quality.
